scope: Missing or expired corpse before the native login LoadCorpse component
finding: No production defect found in the exercised expiry/recovery paths. Existing Player::LoadCorpse calls ResurrectPlayer(0.5f) when a dead player has no cached corpse. This commit adds regression coverage and audit only.
checks: Test-CorpseRestartNative.ps1 -VerifyReleaseBinary passed. Two independent native processes share only disposable corpse SQL; writer uses real KillPlayer/BuildPlayerRepop/SaveToDB for six distinct corpses, then removes cache objects without deleting SQL and exits.

Writer supplies two explicitly old timestamps via SQL UNIX_TIMESTAMP(NOW())-259260. Reader executes the actual CHAR_DEL_OLD_CORPSES prepared statement with the startup age parameter 3*DAY, waits for writes, and verifies only those two corpses plus the synthetic bones row are deleted. Actual CHAR_SEL_CORPSES independently excludes bones before cleanup.

To represent aging after startup SQL, reader ages two remaining SQL rows before native LoadCorpses hydrates them. Actual ObjectAccessor::RemoveOldCorpses removes both expired cache entries and SQL rows while retaining both fresh corpses. This controlled age input does not wait three days or replace native expiry decisions.

Native Corpse::IsExpired returns false exactly at three days and true one second later for each writer PvE/PvP corpse. Native bones return false at five minutes and true one second later. SQL uses its real wall clock; its exact boundary is inspected in the prepared SQL rather than asserted using a racing database/client clock.

Five new socketless Player inputs cover two startup-expired corpses, two runtime-expired corpses and an owner with no corpse ever created. Native LoadCorpse restores alive state at 500/1000 health, removes 8326 and PLAYER_FLAGS_GHOST, leaves no corpse and adds no resurrection sickness. The Night Elf case first asserts native 20584 exists and then is removed by recovery.

Repeated living LoadCorpse preserves deliberately changed health321 and creates no corpse, proving no repeated half-health reset. The two fresh PvE/PvP controls stay dead on LoadCorpse, retain identity/location/time/appearance, survive repeat-save without duplicate rows, then living LoadCorpse converts/deletes them. Final resurrectable SQL count is zero.

Release check confirms canonical worldserver and actual final-link game.lib hashes match the native run and retains the exception-bounded field15 uint64 startup identity check. ObjectAccessor.cpp was added to native freshness dependencies; startup World.cpp and prepared CharacterDatabase.cpp hashes are recorded as evidence.

Both native runs passed; final run additionally asserts that the Night Elf speed aura was actually applied. No production C++ or SQL migration changed, so canonical binaries were not rebuilt and no background servers were launched. Disposable schema-only auth/character databases and scratch SQL user were removed by the wrapper.

limits: This is native code/data verification, not client verification. Player ghost state is explicitly supplied to fresh socketless Players; aggregate Player::LoadFromDB and authenticated network login are not invoked. Character tables remain empty in this two-process fixture.

Corpse persistence, startup cleanup, runtime cleanup and native login recovery are exercised. Persisted character health/flags/aura reload after this recovery is not newly verified here; earlier saved-field logout/relog component audits retain their own scope.
Runtime expiry inputs are hydrated after startup cleanup; this does not model concurrent expiry while a Player is already online. No new behavior is claimed for that separate case.

Actual cold-client login, movement, visibility, resurrection UI, camera/pet state and corpse/bones appearance remain pending client checks. Existing audits and their observed failures remain unchanged.
